data.title: Sweetgreen Stock (SG) Slumps as Investors Leave Their Greens Over Food Illness Outbreak
data.description:
Shares in salad group Sweetgreen (SG) wilted 14% in premarket trading today as investors fretted about the impact of the U.S. cyclosporiasis food poisoning outbreak on its sales.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Uncertain Pace of Recovery

Yesterday, Sweetgreen presenting its Q2 earnings report, said that it had seen reduced consumer demand for fresh prepared foods due to the multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis since mid-July. The pace and timing of recovery remain uncertain, it said.

It now expects a 7% and 8% decline in annual same-store sales, compared with its previous forecast for a 2% to 4% drop.

The current outbreak, tied to recalled iceberg lettuce from central Mexico, has led some U.S. consumers to buy less lettuce and avoid some restaurant chains as the outbreak raises concerns about food safety. It is reportedly one of the largest outbreaks caused by foodborne illnesses in recent U.S. history.

America is in the midst of its worst year on record for a cyclosporiasis outbreak. Since May 1, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed or is investigating more than 18,000 cases of the illness in 45 states, and has reported 423 hospitalizations.

The illness, which can be contracted by consuming food — typically raw fruits and vegetables — or water contaminated with feces, can cause diarrhea, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.

No Lettuce Link

Sweetgreen, however, reiterated in its results that it does not use iceberg lettuce on its menu and has had no indication from U.S. health authorities or its suppliers that it is linked to the outbreak. Despite this its shares have slumped 15% in the last three months.

data.title: ByteDance Is Building a 10T Parameter AI Model to Take On Anthropic's Mythos
data.description:
ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, is developing a new artificial intelligence (AI) system with 10 trillion parameters that could rival Anthropic's flagship Mythos model. According to reports, the model is now in pre-training, which typically lasts three to six months before it is released.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction NVDA bears now have this Tradr ETF

ByteDance Targets One of the World's Largest AI Models

According to reports, ByteDance's upcoming model would be more than three times larger than Chinese startup Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model, which has 2.8 trillion parameters. It would also be close in size to Anthropic's advanced Mythos model, based on industry estimates.

Notably, parameters are used to measure how much an AI model learns during training to recognize patterns and perform tasks. While more parameters usually mean a larger model, they do not always make it more capable.

Meanwhile, industry estimates suggest Anthropic's Mythos 5 has about 8 trillion parameters, while Fable 5 has around 5 trillion. However, neither Anthropic nor ChatGPT creator OpenAI has officially disclosed the size of their latest AI models, making direct comparisons difficult.

ByteDance Accelerates China's AI Race

ByteDance is joining a growing group of Chinese AI firms to build trillion-parameter models. Before the release of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Chinese AI and tech companies like Meituan and DeepSeek led the country's AI sector with models containing about 1.6 trillion parameters.

However, ByteDance's latest project now adds to China's push to build larger and more advanced AI models as competition with U.S. AI labs heat up. The company has also joined hands with Chinese tech firm Unitree Robotics to move beyond AI models and build physical humanoid robots.

What Is the Best AI Stock to Buy? 

ByteDance is still a private company with no publicly traded stock yet. However, investors looking to explore AI stocks can consider top players such as Nvidia (NVDA), Meta Platforms (META), and Google (GOOGL). data.title: Super Micro Stock Falls Before Earnings After Elon Musk Made a Big AI Announcement. What Did He Say?
data.description:
Super Micro Computer stock (SMCI) fell 3.1% to $29.38 on Thursday following comments made by Elon Musk earlier in the week. During SpaceX's (SPCX) earnings call late Tuesday, August 4, Musk announced that his companies, including SpaceX and xAI, would build their AI infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia (NVDA) chips going forward.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction WDC bulls now have this Tradr ETF

As a result, his statement created a lot of concern across the market regarding demand for other tech hardware providers. While Nvidia shares rose on the news, rival chip and server makers took a hit as investors feared a shift away from non-Nvidia suppliers. Investors became worried that server and hardware partners could lose key orders. This caused trade volume in SMCI stock to hit 26.3 million shares.

"Going forward, we have decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture," stated Elon Musk during the SpaceX call.

SMCI Could Be Overpriced

Outside of the comments from Elon Musk, regular trading pressure added to Thursday's drop. After SMCI stock surged in prior weeks, many buyers decided to cash out their short-term profits.

At the same time, traders worry SMCI could be overpriced. The core problem is that the stock price may already reflect all the company's expected growth for the next few quarters. When the market already prices in all the expected growth ahead of time, the stock struggles to climb much higher, even when actual sales results look good.

That is why several Wall Street banks prefer to wait on the sidelines. Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh, rated 5-star, recently dropped his price target to $34 from $44. Citigroup analyst Asiya Merchant, also rated 5-star, set her target at $33. Across the board, analysts hold a consensus "Hold" rating with an average price target of $38.40.

SMCI's Sales Orders Support Upcoming Earnings Growth

Despite the recent price fall, Super Micro Computer reports its Fiscal fourth-quarter results on Tuesday, August 11. Wall Street expects the company to report earnings of $0.68 per share, which marks a 65.9% jump compared to last year.

In addition, quarterly sales estimates sit at $11 billion, representing a 91% increase from the prior year. A record backlog of server orders and solid results from partner Western Digital (WDC) show that data center demand remains high. Consequently, the August 11 earnings release will test whether real profits can help SMCI stock recover from its recent drop.

Is SMCI a Good Buy Right Now?

On TipRanks, Super Micro Computer's stock (SMCI) has a Hold consensus, based on 12 analysts issuing ratings in the past three months. This is based on three Buys, eight Holds, and one Sell rating. The average 12-month SMCI stock price target is $38.40, implying about 30.7% upside potential from the current price levels. data.title: SK Hynix Stock (SKHY) Keeps Dropping Despite $38B Factory Move to Boost Chip Capacity
data.description:
Shares in South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (SKHY) edged lower in pre-market trading today despite setting out $38 billion plans to expand two factories and double its production capacity.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Growing Demand For Memory

The world's second-largest memory chip maker said it will build a new DRAM manufacturing facility in Yongin, South Korea and a NAND fabrication plant in Cheongiu. The move it said comes in response to "the continuously growing demand for memory in the AI era" and will help ease a global shortage of chips.

"This investment is a decision aimed at ensuring we do not miss opportunities as the market grows," an SK Hynux spokesperson added. "By proactively securing production capacity, we will establish ourselves as a key AI infrastructure partner that contributes to the stability of the global AI semiconductor supply chain."

SK Hynix said that the new Yongin Y2 will be the second of four fabs planned at the Yongin semiconductor cluster. It intends to begin construction in July next year, targeting June 2029 for opening the first cleanroom en route to producing high-bandwidth memory and other next-generation DRAM. The Cheongju M17 expansion will begin in February and its first cleanroom is targeted for the end of 2028.

Meeting Investor Concerns

DRAM (Dynamic Random-Access Memory) chips are fast working memory that helps servers and computers process active data quickly. NAND chips are flash memory used in solid-state drives (SSDs) for long-term data storage.

Overall appetite for SK's chips is expected to continue with industry estimates that DRAM manufacturers are only meeting between 75% to 80% of global demand. SK Hynix also continues to innovate bringing HBM4 samples to leading AI chip designers in the second half of this, with reportedly mass production of both HBM4 and HBM4E slated for 2027.  

However, some investors have been concerned that even though the company's production capacity is sold out through 2027 and it is sealing a number of long-term deals with customers that profit margins are sustainable.

data.title: BX, APO, KKR: Private Equity Stocks Wobble After Report Flags Hacker Threat
data.description:
Shares in leading asset managers and private equity firms Blackstone (BX), Apollo Global (APO), and KKR (KKR) struggled to eke out meaningful gains early Friday. This followed a report by Reuters that these firms and others have recently come under the focus of hackers.

U.S. Financial Services Firms Come Under Hackers' Radar

According to the news outlet, its review of data from Google (GOOGL) and online sources revealed the trend. It said hackers created fake websites to steal passwords from company employees.

Other private equity firms targeted include Bain Capital, TPG (TPG), and Clearlake Capital. Not left out, financial services firms such as hedge fund manager Bridgewater Associates, exchange operator CME Group (CME), and credit rating agency Moody's (MCO) were also targeted, the report said.

However, the news agency could not confirm which of the firms were successfully hacked.

Google Flags Use of 'Vishing' by Hackers

In a report published on Thursday, Google Threat Intelligence Group (CTIG) said it continues to track cybercrime group UNC6671. It pointed to its earlier report released in May. The report details the hacker group's recent focus on financial services, private equity, and professional services companies.

According to CTIG, UNC6671 continues to rely on voice phishing (vishing) to target employees of large organizations. Its members pretend to be IT helpdesk staff who want to conduct urgent and mandatory security updates.

"Significantly, the threat actor often contacts employees via their personal mobile devices. These calls lure victims to spoofed login portals where Adversary-in-the-Middle infrastructure intercepts credentials and multi-factor authentication tokens," CTIG explained.

Google Says Hacker Group Is Expanding

UNC6671 emerged in early 2026, according to CTIG. The group originally operated under the name BlackFile. However, rather than disband, the group has expanded. It now operates under multiple names such as Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon.

According to CTIG, the group has conducted several hacks where they stole data and demanded payment not to leak them. The group usually attempts to steal data from cloud apps such as Microsoft's (MSFT) Microsoft 365 and Okta (OKTA).

However, Google did not identify which firms were successfully hacked.

Which Private Equity Stock Is the Best Buy?

Of the four private equity stocks highlighted in this article, KKR (KKR) and TPG (TPG) tie for performance. They both currently offer about 23% upside and are rated Strong Buy based on analysts' consensus.

What's more, they both have a TipRank Smart Score of 10. This is based on an average price target of $126.92 for KKR and $59.90 for TPG.
